item.title: Testing the Unitarity of Three-Flavor Neutrino Mixing above the GUT Scale
item.description: arXiv:2611.33180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how physics between the grand-unification and Planck scales affects neutrino mixing in the standard three-flavor framework, distinguishing genuine non unitarity from unitary shifts of the mixing parameters. First, we show that heavy gauge singlet states at or above the grand-unification scale induce deviations from unitarity of the effective (3\times3) Pontecorvo Maki Nakagawa Sakata (PMNS) matrix, suppressed by the ratio of the light-neutrino mass to the heavy mass. The resulting effects are estimated to be of order (10^{-27}), far below current oscillation constraints. Second, we examine the impact of a flavor-blind dimension-five Weinberg operator suppressed by a high-energy scale (\Lambda). This operator modifies the neutrino mass matrix and shifts the mixing angles while preserving the exact unitarity of the PMNS matrix. Using the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit parameters for normal mass ordering, including the Dirac CP-violating phase, and numerically diagonalizing the corrected complex-symmetric mass matrix, we find that the shift in (\theta_{12}) can reach approximately (0.12^\circ) at the Planck scale for a quasi-degenerate neutrino spectrum, compared with (0.011^\circ) for normal ordering. The corrections increase as (1/\Lambda), reaching approximately (6.5^\circ) for normal ordering near the grand-unification scale, where perturbation theory becomes unreliable for the quasi-degenerate spectrum. Since the Weinberg operator acts entirely within the active three-flavor sector, it introduces no additional non-unitarity parameters; instead, the correlated shifts of the three mixing angles are governed by a single parameter. Our results demonstrate that tests of active-flavor probability conservation cannot directly constrain this high-scale contribution. Its phenomenological signatures must instead be sought in the correlated modifications of the neutrino mixing parameters.
item.dc:creator: Bipin Singh Koranga, Samrat Vashisht

item.title: From nested soft-collinear subtraction to NNLO QCD predictions with large language models
item.description: arXiv:2611.33279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate whether large language models can construct reliable and efficient codes for computing NNLO QCD corrections to collider processes, starting from the general formula derived within the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme. We use Higgs production in weak-boson fusion with and without an additional jet to compare numerical implementations by large language models, subject to various degrees of supervision, against a human-written reference code.
item.dc:creator: Federica Devoto, Kirill Melnikov, Ivan Novikov, Raoul R\"ontsch, Chiara Signorile-Signorile, Davide Maria Tagliabue, Matteo Tresoldi

item.title: Parton structure of mesonic states with tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.33280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for a pion-like isospin triplet in the two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model in (1+1) dimensions. Four-fermion interactions bind the mesons without confinement. Using staggered fermions and a charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian, we prepare the bound states and compute light-cone correlators by real-time evolution. The resulting quark and antiquark PDFs obey the expected isospin relations under $u \leftrightarrow d$ exchange between charged pions and exhibit equal u and d distributions in the neutral pion. A flavor-independent antisymmetrization of the field ordering removes the vacuum-subtracted anticommutator contribution and restores charge-conjugation relations in both the correlators and PDFs across the triplet within numerical accuracy. These results provide benchmarks for quantum simulations of the partonic structure of the meson.
item.dc:creator: Jack Y. Araz, Yamil Cahuana Medrano, Peter L. Nguyen, Zhong-Bo Kang, Jian-Wei Qiu, David Richards, Nobuo Sato, Marco Zaccheddu, Jia-Yue Zhang

item.title: Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger: The $\Delta(1232)$ Resonance in Supernova QCD Axion Emission
item.description: arXiv:2611.33292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The high-energy tail of supernova axion emission controls searches whose response grows with axion energy. We identify a novel production channel, in which the axion is emitted through an intermediate $\Delta(1232)$ resonance, which adds a hard component to the spectrum. We calculate the axion production rate from nucleon-nucleon Bremsstrahlung in chiral effective field theory through next-to-leading order. Including the $\Delta(1232)$ roughly doubles the luminosity at one second after bounce and increases the number of escaping axions above $200$ MeV by a factor of about $3$ over the first nine seconds, relative to the nucleon-only calculation. Adding this new production channel roughly doubles $\gamma$-ray counts from conversion in the progenitor's magnetic field and increases water-Cherenkov counts by about an order of magnitude through its combined effects on emission and absorption. The same hard component can mimic a higher core temperature or thermal-pion emission in $\gamma$-ray spectral fits. The $\Delta(1232)$ resonance is therefore crucial for predicting supernova axion signals and interpreting their spectra.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Arcangeli, Konstantin Springmann, Michael Stadlbauer, Stefan Stelzl, Andreas Weiler

item.title: Physics-informed neural networks for quark Dyson--Schwinger equations and propagator singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.33482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a physics-informed neural-network (PINN) framework for solving the rainbow-truncated quark Dyson--Schwinger equation at real and complex momenta. The resulting dressing functions agree closely with conventional iterative solutions. We investigate the singularity structure of the quark propagator using two complementary methods. Analytic continuation of a PINN trained on the real momentum axis estimates the locations of poles and further reveals three complex-conjugate pole pairs. An independent reconstruction using PINN-parametrized spectral densities and a single pole pair yields $q=-0.146\pm0.391i~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. The agreement between the two methods substantially strengthens confidence in the properties of the leading singularities. Both spectral densities change sign, and the negative regions of the vector density and the complex poles indicate a violation of reflection positivity, consistent with quark confinement. Finally, we use the extracted poles and residues to calculate their contributions to two order parameters at finite quark chemical potential, the chiral condensate and the quark number density.
item.dc:creator: Xin-Peng Li, Zhong-Hua Huang

item.title: Divergence-type hydrodynamics of radial oscillations in viscous neutron stars
item.description: arXiv:2611.33537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on a simplified model of a viscous neutron star in the Newtonian limit coupled to a quadratic dissipative fluid theory of divergence type with bulk viscosity only, we explore the impact of nonlinear effects on the evolution of radial perturbations, and compare it with the results of linear hydrodynamics. For high values of the bulk viscosity $\zeta_B \gtrsim 5\times 10^{31}$ g/cm/s, the linear theory develops growing oscillations, which do appear in the quadratic theory but at much higher values of $\zeta_B$. The quadratic theory shows stronger damping of oscillations, longer decay rates of non-hydrodynamic modes and also a ``stiffer'' evolution of radial perturbations that results in less deformation. These results suggest that nonlinear effects may be relevant to capture the dynamics of the long-lived non-hydrodynamic modes present at high $\zeta_B$.
item.dc:creator: J. Peralta-Ramos

item.title: Determination of the strong coupling constant from the R ratio obtained in KEDR and BESIII experiments
item.description: arXiv:2611.33633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The experimental data collected by the KEDR and BESIII collaborations at energies below the charm quark threshold are compared with the massless QCD expressions for the $e^+e^-$ annihilation R-ratio truncated at different orders of perturbation theory. The fits demonstrate the dependence of the extracted $\alpha_s(M_Z)$ values on the orders of truncation of the corresponding approximations.
item.dc:creator: Korneliy Todyshev, Andrei Kataev

item.title: Singly-strange hidden-bottom and double-bottom molecular pentaquarks
item.description: arXiv:2611.33708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by the observation of the singly-strange hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_{\psi s}^{\Lambda}(4459)$ and $P_{\psi s}^{\Lambda}(4338)$, we present a systematic investigation of the mass spectra of the singly-strange hidden-bottom and double-bottom molecular pentaquarks arising from the $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}B^{(*)}$ and $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ interactions. Using the one-boson-exchange model, we derive the effective potentials for the $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}B^{(*)}$ systems by exchanging light mesons. The effective potentials for the corresponding $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ systems are then obtained via the $G$-parity rule. By solving the coupled-channel Schr\"odinger equation with $S$-$D$ wave mixing and coupled-channel effects, we search for loosely bound states with all possible isospin and spin-parity quantum numbers. Our results show that the $\Xi_b B$ state with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b B^*$ states with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$ and $0(3/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b^\prime B$ state with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b^* B$ state with $I(J^P)=0(3/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b^\prime B^*$ states with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$ and $0(3/2^-)$, and the $\Xi_b^* B^*$ states with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$, $0(3/2^-)$, and $0(5/2^-)$ are identified as promising candidates of the singly-strange hidden-bottom molecular pentaquarks. Their $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ partners are likewise predicted to be the singly-strange double-bottom molecular pentaquark candidates. These predictions provide concrete targets for future experimental searches for exotic hadrons in the bottom sector, for example at LHCb.
item.dc:creator: Fu-Lai Wang, Jia-Ning Cui, Rui Chen, Xiang Liu

item.title: Heavy quark drag coefficient using phonon-heavy quark EFT
item.description: arXiv:2611.33709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The description of heavy quarks inside the QGP medium, especially at low momenta, remains challenging from first principles due to the strong coupling and large gluon occupation numbers. An alternative description in terms of perturbative degrees of freedom treats the interactions of heavy quarks with the collective excitations of the medium in the form of phonons. This description is derived as an effective field theory (EFT) and therefore allows for a naturally occurring power counting of the allowed interactions. This EFT has already been established in our previous work, where we derived the phonon-heavy quark interactions and calculated their thermal scattering cross section. In this work, we use these results, together with the heavy quark expansion, to calculate the heavy quark drag coefficient. Subsequently, we compare our results with the drag coefficient obtained from AdS/CFT calculations to determine the previously unknown Wilson coefficients for the quark-phonon coupling. Additionally, we determine the same Wilson coefficients by matching the EFT result for the drag force at low momenta with the QCD result at high momenta. Finally, we will compare our results with experimentally determined heavy quark diffusion coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kirchner, Noah Koliadko, Berndt Mueller, Jyotirmoy Roy

item.title: Higgsino dark matter explanation of LZ high-recoil event from deflected AMSB with $U(1)_X$ generated $\mu$ term
item.description: arXiv:2611.33787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the recent LZ high-recoil event, we propose to study the Higgsino dark matter in a supersymmetric $U(1)_X$ framework with one charged visible singlet. The gauge symmetry forbids the bare Higgs bilinear and the cubic $S^3$ while allowing the singlet interaction that generates an effective Higgsino mass after symmetry breaking. We present the six-state neutralino mixing matrix, including the $U(1)_X$ gaugino and the singlino, and the resulting neutral Higgsino mass splitting. Different deflected-anomaly-mediated parameter regimes provide the soft-mass hierarchies needed for light, 1.1 TeV and heavy Higgsino candidates. The cosmological consequences of the messenger sector in deflected AMSB can affect greatly the thermal history of the dark matter. Late messenger decays can supplement an underabundant thermal population or dilute an overabundant one through entropy production. These possibilities are governed by a common final-yield relation: a dominating messenger must have sufficiently suppressed Higgsino production for net dilution to succeed. We organise the 500 GeV, 1.1 TeV and 100 TeV reference regimes around this condition. Direct-detection and solar-capture constraints are discussed as tests of the resulting spectrum and final abundance. The elastic bino- or singlino-like interpretation of the same event is also realized in this spectrum: the Higgsino asymmetry $|X_A|\simeq10^{-2}$ that a $248\keV$ recoil requires arises without tuning, with a spin-dependent rate lying close to the present experimental sensitivity.
item.dc:creator: Ke-Lin Li, Fei Wang

item.title: Collisional dynamics of neutrino flavor conversion: angular structures, inhomogeneity, and decoherence
item.description: arXiv:2611.33815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-interacting neutrino gases exhibit collective behavior, in which additional incoherent collisions can induce collisional neutrino-flavor instability. We investigate the effects of energy dependence, anisotropy, and spatial inhomogeneity on the resulting flavor conversion through linear stability analysis and nonlinear quantum kinetic simulations. We find contrasting wavenumber dependences for the near/gapless and far/gapped branches, with maximum growth rates at collision-scale shifted wavenumbers and at collective-scale wavenumbers, respectively. Their eigenvectors reveal distinct energy and angular structures, which are reflected in the subsequent establishment of flavor swap and equipartition. The nonlinear evolution also features secondary flavor growth associated with changes in the stability of collective modes as the neutrino background evolves. Despite the spreading of flavor coherence across spatial scales due to nonlinear mode coupling, collisional decoherence tends to limit the development of spatial inhomogeneities, leaving the neutrino populations nearly homogeneous. These findings represent a step towards understanding and predicting the nonlinear flavor evolution of dense neutrino gases interacting with their surroundings, particularly in explosive astrophysical environments.
item.dc:creator: Masamichi Zaizen

item.title: Origin of flavour cancellations in thermal leptogenesis
item.description: arXiv:2611.33862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In thermal leptogenesis with three hierarchical heavy neutrinos $N_1$, $N_2$ and $N_3$, the baryon asymmetry can be the small remainder of large contributions that cancel. Interference terms in the CP asymmetry are known to contribute to the final asymmetry through flavour-dependent washout. However, it remains unclear where the cancellation occurs, how large the interference contribution is, and how the accuracy of approximate equations changes when this information is lost. We split the CP asymmetry into diagonal and off-diagonal parts in the charged-lepton basis and evolve them with Standard Model transport equations. We find that the cancellation occurs mainly between the diagonal and off-diagonal parts of the same heavy neutrino, and that it is caused by flavour-dependent washout. We also find that the interference between the lepton state produced in the decay and the states orthogonal to it typically accounts for most of the $N_2$ and $N_3$ contribution. Approximations that reduce the CP asymmetry to flavour populations turn out to miss most of this contribution, whereas density-matrix equations with the full CP-asymmetry matrix agree much better.
item.dc:creator: Teruyuki Kitabayashi

item.title: Revisiting the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in an anisotropic quark-gluon plasma
item.description: arXiv:2611.33959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in a quark-gluon plasma with a small momentum-space anisotropy. Within the Braaten-Thoma framework, we obtain the hard contribution in closed form and reduce the soft contribution to one-dimensional integrals. Our result demonstrates analytically that, at linear order in the anisotropy, the dependence on the artificial separation scale cancels between the two contributions. By considering the unnormalized anisotropic distribution together with two variants that hold either the parton number density or the energy density at its isotropic value, we find that the angle-dependent part of the anisotropy correction is identical in all three cases and is proportional to the quadrupole $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is the angle between the heavy-quark velocity and the anisotropy direction. In addition, the sign of the anisotropy correction, which determines whether the energy loss is enhanced or suppressed relative to the isotropic result, depends jointly on the quark speed, coupling, and propagation angle. In particular, at fixed energy density, only the quadrupole term survives. For a positive coefficient of $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, the correction enhances the energy loss for $\cos^2\alpha>1/3$ and suppresses it for $\cos^2\alpha<1/3$, with the opposite behavior for a negative coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Mingda Cai, Yun Guo, Enke Wang

item.title: Coherent quantum-circuit simulation of Mueller dipole branching at small $x$: multiplicity fluctuations and DIS phenomenology
item.description: arXiv:2611.33979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mueller dipole branching at small $x$ is a stochastic process in which splitting rates depend on transverse geometry. We construct a coherent quantum circuit for a regulated finite-state version of this process. Poisson-clock uniformization controls the number of updates, while orthogonal event-history registers retain the splitting paths, including those leading to the same final configuration. The circuit prepares transition amplitudes from local splitting rates rather than loading a precomputed evolved distribution. Its statevector multiplicity probabilities reproduce the truncated-clock Markov result to numerical precision and agree with the full continuous-time Markov-chain benchmark within approximately $7\times10^{-4}$. To examine fluctuations beyond the small circuit, we independently simulate the Mueller cascade with continuous transverse coordinates. At the largest rapidity studied, its normalized fourth factorial moment is $1.81$, compared with $2.84$ for an equal-mean Yule process. We also determine multiplicity entropies and correlations between dipole-size sectors. Applying a fixed negative-binomial dipole-to-charged-particle response reproduces the rising trend of the H1 charged-particle multiplicity entropy toward smaller $x$, but does not fully describe the measured multiplicity distributions. These results demonstrate an explicit coherent encoding of finite-state dipole branching and clarify its relation to continuous-cascade fluctuations and DIS phenomenology.
item.dc:creator: Wei Kou, Xurong Chen

item.title: Determining the kaon distribution amplitudes by fitting the $D\to K$ transition form factor to investigate the equivalence of two chiral LCSR frameworks
item.description: arXiv:2611.34007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we fit the $D\to K$ vector transition form factor (TFF) to the BESIII experimental data using a Monte Carlo (MC) method. We also calculate the TFF using QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSRs) with left-and right-handed chiral currents. For the TFF derived using the right-handed chiral current, the key input is the kaon twist-2 distribution amplitude (DA), for which we consider three models: the power-law parametrization ($\mathrm{R1}$), the truncated Gegenbauer expansion ($\mathrm{R2}$), and the light-cone harmonic oscillator (LCHO) model ($\mathrm{R3}$). The parameters of these models are determined by fitting the corresponding TFF predictions to the MC-fit results. For the TFF derived using the left-handed chiral current, the dominant input is the kaon twist-3 DA ($\mathrm{L4}$), which is constructed within the LCHO framework. Its parameters are determined from theoretical constraints rather than from the fit. In the large-recoil region, the resulting TFF are $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R1}}=0.7381^{+0.0180}_{-0.0194}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R2}}=0.7320^{+0.0178}_{-0.0192}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R3}}=0.7324^{+0.0180}_{-0.0191}$, and $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{L4}}=0.7343^{+0.0459}_{-0.0573}$. We then calculate the decay widths and branching fractions of the semileptonic decays $D\to K e\nu_e$ and extract the CKM matrix element $|V_{cs}|$. Finally, we predict the two important ratios, $\mathcal{R}_{\pi^-/K^-}^{e}$ and $\mathcal{R}_{\pi^0/K^0}^{e}$. All the obtained results are consistent with existing experimental measurements and theoretical predictions.
item.dc:creator: Fang-Ping Peng, Sheng-Bo Wu, Hai-Bing Fu

item.title: Non-perturbative charm production from color ropes in relativistic heavy ion collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.34009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present results on charm production in nucleus-nucleus reactions in the energy range $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5$-$20$ GeV, obtained with the SMASH transport approach extended to include color rope formation. We show that string fusion may provide a substantial additional non-perturbative source of charm production. This may help to explain the apparent charm enhancement (above the pQCD expectations) at low transverse momenta. Our predicted neutral $D$-meson yields are consistent with current experimental constraints and may provide valuable insights for upcoming data by the NA61/SHINE collaboration.
item.dc:creator: Carl B. Rosenkvist, Marcus Bleicher

item.title: Towards Quark-Gluon Correlations in Pion from the Dyson-Schwinger Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.34030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twist-3 distributions encode quark-gluon correlations, and the pion's chiral-odd $e(x)$ is the simplest of them. QCD fixes its lowest moments exactly, yet the only rainbow-ladder (RL) calculation of $e(x)$ omitted the Wilson line and violated the equation-of-motion (EOM) sum rule for the first moment. We show that the discrepancy is not a failure of RL but of the omitted link: at first order in the coupling, the link contributes three classes of planar diagrams that cancel the EOM violation class by class, so the sum rule is restored exactly in RL. The resulting zeroth and first moments are complete RL results. The genuine twist-3 component changes sign near $x=0.45$, and the Wilson line more than doubles its magnitude in the negative region. This identifies the Wilson line as the missing ingredient in the RL description of $e(x)$ and sets the stage for a full resummation of the $gA$ expansion.
item.dc:creator: Zanbin Xing, Jiayin Kang, Lei Chang

item.title: Black hole accretion flows as dark matter bolometers
item.description: arXiv:2611.34172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Astrophysical systems provide powerful probes of dark matter interactions, complementing direct-detection searches. We propose using accretion flows of the supermassive black hole as a bolometer for light DM. The kinetic energy of sub-MeV dark matter in the black hole gravitational potential can remain below the thermal energy of the plasma electrons. The colder dark matter population can therefore absorb energy through elastic scattering, cooling the electrons and modifying their emission spectrum. We integrate dark matter cooling into the advection-dominated accretion flow around M87$^{*}$ and solve the full set of thermodynamic equations to obtain the resulting temperature profile and radio-to-millimeter emission. By comparing the predicted spectrum with observations accompanying the Event Horizon Telescope campaign, we use, for the first time, the thermal energy balance of the hot accretion flow to constrain DM-electron scattering, obtaining stringent limits on keV-to-MeV DM for both heavy and light mediators.
item.dc:creator: Ran Ding, Ningqiang Song, Cong Zhang

item.title: Lower Bound on the Lightest Neutrino Mass with Resonant Neutrino Self-Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.34213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show the possibility of using the resonant $s$-channel scattering of ultra high energy astrophysical neutrinos with the low energy cosmic neutrino background to put a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass. This can be realized and illustrated by neutrino self-interactions with a light scalar mediator of $\mathcal O(1)$ MeV mass. After analyzing the kinematics and cross section features of the $s$-channel resonance, we derive from first principles the double transport equations with double regeneration terms for the coupled evolution of neutrinos and anti-neutrinos. The simulated event spectrum is then compared with the HESE 7.5 year data observed at IceCube to give a clear lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass.
item.dc:creator: Shao-Feng Ge, Joao Paulo Pinheiro, Shaoyang Qin, Ruitao Sun, Oleg Titov

item.title: Complete NNLO QCD Calculations of $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)$ Form Factors and Semileptonic Decays
item.description: arXiv:2611.34263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the first complete next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD calculation of all 34 vector, axial-vector, tensor, and axial-tensor form factors for the four $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)$ transitions within nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization. Using automated multi-loop techniques based on \texttt{FeynCalc} and \texttt{AMFlow}, we provide a dataset with at least 40 significant digits at 35 exact rational points in the $(m_b,m_c,q^2)$ parameter space, covering $q^2\in[-10,10]~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. In the spacelike region ($q^2<0$) and near $q^2=0$, the NLO corrections typically enhance the LO form factors by $\mathcal{O}(70\%)$, while the NNLO corrections amount to $\mathcal{O}(20\%)$ of the NLO predictions and substantially reduce the renormalization-scale dependence, demonstrating good perturbative convergence. In contrast, fixed-order NRQCD predictions suffer from threshold instabilities and become less reliable at higher timelike $q^2$. We therefore extrapolate the form factors to the full physical region via $z$-series fits to the NRQCD results at spacelike and near-zero $q^2$, finding broad agreement with the latest lattice QCD results for $B_c\to J/\psi$. With the resulting NRQCD+$z$-series form factors, we predict the decay widths, branching fractions, and lepton-flavor-universality (LFU) ratios for $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)\,\ell\nu_\ell$ ($\ell=e,\mu,\tau$) at LO, NLO, and NNLO. Higher-order corrections substantially enhance the absolute rates but largely cancel in the ratios, whose uncertainties are dominated by the choice of fitting points. In particular, our NNLO central prediction $\mathcal{R}(B_c\to J/\psi)=0.2836$ lies between the latest lattice QCD determination and the most recent LHCb measurement.
item.dc:creator: Wei Tao, Zhen-Jun Xiao, Ruilin Zhu, Qin Chang

item.title: Isospin violating decay of D wave charmonia
item.description: arXiv:2611.34394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The experimental observations of $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ enrich the $D$ wave charmonia family. In our previous work the decays of $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ to isospin conserved non-$D\bar D$ hadronic decays are well studied. Since the isospin violated decay channel $\psi(3770)\to J/\psi \pi$ is measured clearly very recently, so in this work we fit the model parameter $\alpha$ through $BR(\psi(3770)\to J/\psi \pi)_{exp}$, then study the contribution of isospin violated decay channels of $\psi(3770)\to h_c\pi$, $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ to $J/\psi\pi$ and $h_c\pi$, respectively. With this range of parameters space, the branching ratio of $\psi(3770)\to h_c\pi$ is estimated to be $(2.7\sim4.4)\times10^{-7}$. The decay widths of $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ to $J/\psi\pi$ and $h_c\pi$ are also estimated. Our results show that the partial width of $\psi(3823)\to J/\psi\pi$ is $1.12\sim1.77$ eV, the value for $\psi(3823)\to h_c\pi$ is $0.71\sim1.04$ eV, and $0.028\sim0.044$ eV for $\psi(3842)\to J/\psi\pi$, $0.34\sim0.49$ eV for $\psi(3842)\to h_c\pi$, respectively. We hope those values could be tested by further precise measurements from the BES III, Belle II and LHCb Collaborations.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Dao Guo, Qi Wu, Dian-Yong Chen

item.title: Lighting up LZ with Loopy Transitions in a leptophilic Dark Sector
item.description: arXiv:2611.34438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the direct detection phenomenology and cosmology of a multicomponent dark sector with a leptophilic t-channel portal. The coupling to right-handed Standard Model leptons is mediated by a charged vector-like fermion, allowing both a scalar and a vector dark candidate to connect to the SM through the same mediator. Motivated by the high-energy nuclear-recoil event recently reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, we consider a nearly degenerate dark sector with mass splittings of order a few hundred keV and investigate the resulting inelastic transitions. Concretely, we focus on endothermic scattering of the dark states, which can shift the recoil spectrum towards the high-energy region preferred by LZ while suppressing low-energy events. We scrutinize the effective operators generating the dark-matter-photon coupling, which provides the essential interaction for nuclear recoils. Interestingly, the inelastic transition arises at dimension five whereas elastic scattering on nuclei is induced only at dimension six. This naturally explains the prominence of endothermic scattering compared to its elastic counterpart. We determine the parameter space compatible with the observed dark matter abundance and scrutinize the event rate and signal shape for scattering on xenon. Our results demonstrate that the observation of a single $E_R=248\pm 46$ keV nuclear recoil event in LZ can be accommodated by thermally produced dark matter in a leptophilic dark sector.
item.dc:creator: Simone Biondini, Clara Hofheinz, Stefan Melchin, Lorenzo Tiberi, Stefan Vogl

item.title: Inverted Pendulum in the Sky: Floquet Stabilization of Cosmological Axions
item.description: arXiv:2611.34439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many cosmological scenarios require a scalar field to sit near the top of its potential, which usually requires a fine-tuned initial condition. We ask whether the hilltop of an axion potential can be dynamically stabilized by a rapidly oscillating coupling, as for the inverted pendulum of Kapitza, and to what extent this can reduce the fine-tuning. Using Floquet theory, we determine the stability window of the hilltop and analyze several realizations: an oscillating coupling, a spinning or oscillating second field, and a gyroscopic analogue, an inverted spinning top realized by a sigma model on a squashed three-sphere. In an expanding Universe the stabilized phase lasts for a number of $e$-folds logarithmic in the hierarchy of scales, independently of the cosmological background. Classifying the stabilizers by how their effective frequency redshifts, we show that in these realizations the hilltop cannot both attract the field and leave it frozen by the Hubble friction during radiation or matter domination, and that during inflation the attraction is limited by the Hubble friction and the energy budget. Thus the simple realizations studied here do not generically remove the hilltop fine-tuning. They can instead delay the onset of the oscillation and enhance the relic abundance as $n_\phi/n_{\phi,{\rm std}}\propto(\tilde m/H_c)^{3/2}$ in radiation domination. We discuss the implications for axion dark matter, inflation, quintessence and curvatons.
item.dc:creator: Tokiro Numasawa, Masahito Yamazaki

item.title: Ultralight Dark Matter Spectrum with Gravitational Focusing and Doppler Motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.34464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultralight dark matter can produce signals in experiments through its couplings with the Standard Model particles. The resulting signal spectrum is determined by the phase-space distribution of dark matter, which encodes information about its production mechanism and the history of the local universe. However, the local environmental effects can modify the observed spectrum and should be included in signal modeling to avoid biased parameter estimates. In this work, we investigate how the gravitational focusing by Sun and the Doppler effect due to the detector's motion modify the signal spectrum and affect inferring the underlying dark matter parameters. We analytically estimate the signal significance and perform Bayesian analysis on simulated data to demonstrate their impact.
item.dc:creator: Shao-Feng Ge, Yong Tang, Yue-Hui Yao

item.title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
item.description: arXiv:2611.34475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. The results distinguish conditional state identifiability from operational temperature inference.
item.dc:creator: Jilali Loulijat, Abdallah Slaoui, El Hassan Saidi, Mohamed Gouighri, Berihu Teklu

item.title: Recent Developments in Colibri: A Neural-Network PDF Model and Improved Bayesian Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.34502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present recent developments in Colibri, an open-source framework for flexible fits of parton distribution functions (PDFs). Colibri allows the implementation of any PDF functional form as well as Bayesian, Monte Carlo, and Hessian inference methods, making it particularly well suited for systematic comparisons of model architectures and uncertainty propagation treatments. In these proceedings, we report on two key updates to the framework: the release of colibri-n3fit, an open-source implementation of the neural-network model used by the NNPDF collaboration, and the integration of an upgraded, highly efficient Bayesian sampler, bridging the gap between the computational cost of Bayesian PDF fitting and other uncertainty propagation treatments. Combined, these updates extend Colibri's capabilities to neural-network PDF fits, enabling direct, quantitative Bayesian analyses of the n3fit architecture and opening new avenues for comparative studies.
item.dc:creator: Ella Cole, Valentina Sch\"utze S\'anchez

item.title: Majorana Neutrino Exchange in Free-Baryon $B_1B_2\to ppe^-e^-$ Reactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.34504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The free-baryon reactions $B_1B_2\to pp e^-e^-$ are studied for six nonstrange and strange initial states, with light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange treated in the same baryon-level framework. For light-neutrino exchange, the cross sections scale with the square of the effective Majorana mass $m_{\beta\beta}$. The calculated cross sections increase as the off-shell cutoff $\Delta q^2$ is reduced, especially near threshold and in the hyperon channels, because more of the phase-space region where the squared four-momentum of the exchanged neutrino is close to zero is retained. At $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the six light-neutrino cross sections span $9.28\times10^{-49}$--$1.78\times10^{-45}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $m_{\beta\beta}=30~\mathrm{meV}$ and $\Delta q^2=10^{-2}~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. For heavy-neutrino exchange, the cross sections scale with $\eta_N^2$, where $\eta_N=|U_{eN}|^2/m_N$. The leading propagator correction remains below one percent for $m_N\gtrsim50~\mathrm{GeV}$ over the phase-space region considered. At $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the heavy-neutrino cross sections span $7.55\times10^{-45}$--$1.98\times10^{-41}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $\eta_N=4.0\times10^{-9}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. At higher energies, the two exchange cases give the same CKM-driven channel ordering, with the $nn$ cross section largest. At fixed $\sqrt{s}$, compared with the light-neutrino spectra calculated with $\Delta q^2=10^{-2}~\mbox{GeV}^2$, the heavy-neutrino peaks occur at a smaller squared invariant mass for the proton pair and a larger one for the electron pair. These results extend the free-baryon analogue of neutrinoless double-beta decay to strange initial states and provide theoretical reference results for comparing light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange.
item.dc:creator: Yuan-Guo Xu, Bo Lan, Ben-Hou Xiang, Shuang-Shi Fang, Yi-Bing Zhang, Ru-Min Wang

item.title: Confronting $b \to (s, d)\mu^+ \mu^-$ and $\mathcal{L}_{K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}}$ puzzle in a $U(1)_{B-3L_\mu}$ framework with neutrino phenomenology
item.description: arXiv:2611.34525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current data on several observables in $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ transitions reveal certain discrepancies with Standard Model (SM) predictions. Considering the possibility that these deviations stem from new physics, we explore a $Z^{\prime}$ framework based on $U(1)_{B-3L_\mu}$ model. The parameter space is examined in light of existing constraints from $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ transitions. Within this framework, we show that the quark couplings accommodating $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ anomalies, imprint correlated signatures on the non-leptonic puzzles $\mathcal{L}_{K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}}$ in $B_{s(d)} \to K^{{*}}\bar{K}^{{*}}$ decays. We find that the scenario with both vector and axial-vector contributions of opposite sign is favored by the data compared to pure vector contribution, offering a correlated probe of the underlying new-physics scenario. We further explore the neutrino phenomenology within the same framework in light of current data.
item.dc:creator: Dhiren Panda, Priya Mishra, Manas Kumar Mohapatra, Rukmani Mohanta

item.title: Rational terms and UV counterterms of the SMEFT at next-to-leading order in QCD
item.description: arXiv:2611.34531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the rational terms $R_2$ and the ultraviolet counterterms of the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD without any flavour assumption, for complex Wilson coefficients, massive quarks and a general CKM matrix. We also compute the on-shell renormalisation factors of the quark fields in the presence of flavour mixing. We work with an anticommuting $\gamma_5$ and read closed fermion loops with a single $\gamma_5$ at the operator insertion. The results, also for common flavour assumptions, are provided in electronic form and in a Mathematica package attached to the paper. We use them to build example models for MadGraph5_aMC@NLO and give NLO predictions for representative processes.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Ventura

item.title: Gravity-induced mixing, regeneration and CP violation
item.description: arXiv:2611.34595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The analysis of neutral mesons oscillations perturbed by Earth's gravity reveals a small coupling between flavor oscillations and quarks zitterbewegung. As a result of this small gravity-induced coupling between two very low energy oscillations, the mass eigenstates are no longer the Charge-Parity eigenstates. The three types of observed CP violation effects result from this gravity-induced mixing. The associated violation parameters are predicted in full agreement with the experimental data. Thus gravity-induced CP violation offers the accurate framework to understand the origin of CP symmetry violation in neutral mesons experiments. This origin renews in depth the problem of the required large-scale asymmetric baryogenesis in the early universe. Furthermore, the issues of the small time reversal violation in neutral kaons experiments and of the strong CP problem are fully clarified within this new framework of analysis taking into account gravity.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Marcel Rax

item.title: Entanglement entropy in low x Deep Inelastic Scattering
item.description: arXiv:2611.34604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a 2017 paper by Kharzeev and Levin, it has been proposed that hadronic entropy, extracted from the multiplicity of final state hadrons, provides a measure of entanglement in the proton wave function, observed in Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS) of electrons and protons. In this contribution we discuss how the density matrix of the low x DIS system can give rise to a mixed state and therefore to finite entanglement entropy. We further present recent numerical results on the determination of low x dipole multiplicities, based on the solution of the Levin-Lublinsky evolution equation.
item.dc:creator: Martin Hentschinski

item.title: Tackling the DVCS inverse problem with finite element method
item.description: arXiv:2611.34631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we tackle the problem of shadow GPDs, arising from the non-invertibility of the measured $2\to 2$ exclusive processes at large virtualities (DVCS, TCS and DVMP). This problem arose five years ago as the main source of theoretical uncertainties, potentially dominating experimental ones by orders of magnitude. We show here that the deconvolution ambiguity can be elegantly eliminated by relying on finite element method. The problem is essentially converted at any finite discretisation area $a$ from a non-invertible to an ill-conditioned one. Given experimental uncertainties, this yields a theoretical lower bound on the discretisation area $a_\textrm{min}$, that can be interpreted as the maximal theoretical resolution one can obtain on the reconstruction of the lightcone momentum fractions. Associated with the local polynomial degree $p$, the pair $(a,p)$ provides an insightful and easily understandable regularisation framework, allowing one to systematically improve the description of the momentum fractions dependence of GPDs with the pQCD order at which the hard kernels of exclusive processes are computed.
item.dc:creator: Marija \v{C}ui\'c, C\'edric Mezrag, Jos\'e Manuel Morgado Ch\'avez

item.title: QED corrections to neutron and nuclear $\beta$-decay at order $\alpha^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.34804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute two-loop QED corrections to neutron and nuclear beta decay, including full electron mass dependence and real radiation contributions. The result for the neutron, $\delta_{R,\,\rm static}= ( 29.199 \pm 0.001 )\times 10^{-3}$, implies a factor $\sim 70 $ reduction in the uncertainty of the low-energy radiative corrections compared to previous results obtained in the large energy/small electron-mass limit, $m_e/(m_n-m_p) \to 0$. For superallowed nuclear decays we find that the $Z$-independent order $\alpha^2$ corrections range from $(0.1-0.5) \times 10^{-4}$ i.e., of roughly the expected size and comparable to current uncertainty estimates.
item.dc:creator: Zehua Cao, Richard J. Hill, Ryan Plestid, Peter Vander Griend

item.title: Probing Ultralight Dark Matter at the Electroweak Scale
item.description: arXiv:2611.34808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultralight dark matter provides an explanation for astrophysical evidence for dark matter at all scales. This non-thermal dark matter requires a misalignment mechanism to reproduce the observed matter energy density of the Universe and therefore induce oscillating, time-dependent signals. We determine the sensitivity of current and future collider measurements of the width of the Z and Higgs bosons, and show that CP odd observables such as dipole moments in $Z\to \tau^+\tau^-$ decays provide a better sensitivity to ultralight dark matter than atomic clocks or equivalence principle tests.
item.dc:creator: Martin Bauer, Sreemanti Chakraborti

item.title: Heavy-flavor transverse energy-energy correlators in the color-glass condensate
item.description: arXiv:2611.34815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We calculate the transverse energy--energy correlator (TEEC) for forward heavy-quark pair production in proton--nucleus collisions at leading order within the Color Glass Condensate framework. The calculation retains the heavy--quark mass, exact final-state parton kinematics and full relative azimuthal-angle dependence, without imposing a back-to-back approximation. Within the adopted collinear fragmentation prescription, a complete sum over hadron species in the two heavy-quark fragmentation branches eliminates the fragmentation functions through the momentum sum rule. We present numerical results for charm production at RHIC energies and charm and bottom production at LHC energies, using HERA-constrained McLerran--Venugopalan initial conditions evolved with the running-coupling Balitsky--Kovchegov equation. Relative to proton--proton collisions, the nuclear target suppresses the integrated TEEC per nucleon and shifts the relative angular weight towards configurations farther from back-to-back. The magnitude and angular dependence of these modifications vary with the quark mass, collision kinematics and nuclear geometry. These results illustrate the sensitivity of heavy-flavor energy correlations to nuclear small-$x$ dynamics while reducing their leading collinear fragmentation dependence.
item.dc:creator: Zhong-Bo Kang, Carlos Lamas, Jani Penttala

item.title: Screening of New Abelian Long-Range Forces
item.description: arXiv:2611.34838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how bounds on new $U(1)$ long-range forces, resulting from gauging the Standard Model symmetries $B-L$ and $L_a-L_b$, $a,b=e,\mu,\tau$, are modified if the mediator mass is generated by the Higgs mechanism. Large baryonic and leptonic charges of astronomical bodies displace the Higgs field from its vacuum value, resulting in charge screening. Depending on the $U(1)$ Higgs mass, the screening relaxes the bounds on the new force strength and mediator mass from equivalence principle violation and neutrino oscillations experiments, and eliminates the bounds on the muonic $L_\mu-L_\tau$ force from neutron star binaries.
item.dc:creator: Marco Costa, Andrey Shkerin, Ananda Thomlinson

item.title: Probing the CKM Origin of CP Violation with Paramagnetic EDMs and Rare Kaon Decays
item.description: arXiv:2611.34856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the Standard Model, paramagnetic electric dipole moments (EDMs) are dominated by kaon exchange, which pairs the CP-violating short-distance transition $s\to d\,e^+e^-$ with a CP-conserving weak kaon-nucleon coupling. Long-distance two-photon exchange, which dominates $K_L\to e^+e^-$, gives an electron vertex about thirty-five times larger than the short-distance one and could obscure this origin. We show that it does not: the two-photon vertex conserves CP and must be paired with the CP-violating penguin component of the nucleon coupling, whose relative size is $3\times10^{-4}$, so that electromagnetic corrections stay at the few-percent level. Paramagnetic EDMs therefore measure $\mathrm{Im}(V_{ts}^*V_{td})$ and, together with the CP-violating $S$ wave of $K_S\to\mu^+\mu^-$ and $K_L\to\pi^0\nu\bar\nu$, determine the same imaginary coordinate of a kaon CKM plane with electrons, muons, and neutrinos, without $B$-decay input. Lepton-specific new physics, or CP violation that bypasses kaon exchange, would separate these determinations. Testing their common CKM origin calls for coordinated progress in molecular EDM searches, rare-kaon experiments at LHCb, NA62, and KOTO, and lattice determinations of weak nucleon matrix elements.
item.dc:creator: Giancarlo D'Ambrosio, Luca Di Luzio

item.title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.34888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one. A well-established framework, rooted in the work of Davies and operationalised for particle physics by Gross and Vitells, provides this correction for scans over continuous parameters. Some aspects, however, remain unsettled. The definition of "elsewhere" is ambiguous and ranges from a single distribution to an entire experimental programme. Moreover, the analytical shortcuts of the classical framework do not carry over to searches based on machine learning (ML), which are affected by an implicit post-selection bias that depends on the model's resolution and expressiveness. This review covers the LEE in searches for new physics at colliders, from its statistical foundations to these modern challenges. We discuss the corrections for continuous scans and for multiple discrete tests, illustrated with simple numerical examples, and the interaction between ML and the LEE, which we connect to the broader literature on selective inference. We highlight open problems, including the computational cost of empirical calibration for complex models and the development of analytical shortcuts for ML test statistics, and offer recommendations for reporting discovery significance in both classical and ML-based searches in particle physics.
item.dc:creator: Gaia Grosso, Sergio Rodriguez-Benitez, Louis Lyons

item.title: KEBBABS: Kilometric Enhanced Balloon-Baseline for Axion Birefringence Search
item.description: arXiv:2611.34927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a broadband search for ultralight axion dark matter through the rotation of laser polarization induced by the axion--photon coupling. Two stratospheric balloons flying at altitudes of 30--40 km form a free-space optical link. One balloon sends a linearly polarized beam to the other, which reflects it back to a polarimeter on the first balloon. The long physical baseline provides an alternative to the repeated reflections used in resonant optical cavities. We target axion masses in the range $4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{eV}\lesssim m_a\lesssim10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. The lower edge corresponds to a frequency of about $1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, below which gondola roll about the line of sight can mimic a polarization signal. At $m_a=10^{-14}\,\mathrm{eV}$, a low-cost Pathfinder using flight-demonstrated technology could probe couplings as small as $g_{a\gamma}\simeq2.8\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, about a factor of two below the CAST bound. At the same mass, the Feasible today configuration could probe couplings just below the astrophysical bounds considered here, while the Futuristic configuration could reach $g_{a\gamma}\simeq6.4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, roughly two orders of magnitude below those bounds.
item.dc:creator: Tommaso Feri, Silvia Gasparotto

item.title: ACT Excited: Reconciling Starobinsky and Quadratic Chaotic Inflationary Models with ACT Results via Excited States
item.description: arXiv:2611.28144v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data Release 6 of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, combined with Planck, CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, favours a higher scalar spectral index $n_{s}$ than Planck and a mildly positive running $\alpha_{s}$, putting the Starobinsky model in tension with the data, while the quadratic chaotic model is already excluded by its large tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. We show that relaxing the Bunch--Davies assumption for the initial state of the scalar perturbations can restore agreement without modifying the inflaton potential. Parametrising the Bogoliubov coefficients by an excitation parameter $\chi_{S}$ and a relative phase $2\varphi_{S}$, we derive the shifts of $n_{s}$ and $\alpha_{s}$ induced by their scale dependence and map the regions of the $(\varphi_{S},\chi_{S})$ plane compatible with the $1\sigma$ ACT DR6 ranges, the bound $r<0.038$, and the requirement that the scale of new physics $\Lambda$ exceed the Hubble scale $H$. For the Starobinsky model, a scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ or $\varphi_{S}$ works almost everywhere in this plane: only small neighbourhoods of $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi$ with $\chi_{S}\gtrsim1.22$ are excluded, and a scale-dependent phase fails at $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi/2,\pi$ and at $\chi_{S}=0$, where the required ${\rm d}\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k$ and ${\rm d}^2\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2$ diverge. For the QC model, the excited state must also suppress $r$, which requires $\chi_{S}\gtrsim0.63$ and $\Lambda\lesssim6H$. A scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ must satisfy $|{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k|\gtrsim0.0021$ in both models, and in the QC model we show analytically that $0.0021\lesssim{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k\lesssim0.0058$ and $0.0008\lesssim{\rm d}^2\chi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2\lesssim0.0062$. If the tensor modes remain in the BD state, the scenario also predicts a violation of the consistency relation $r=-8n_{T}$, testable once the tensor power spectrum and its tilt are measured.
item.dc:creator: Amjad Ashoorioon, Abdolreza Yousefi-Sostani

item.title: Unitarization from Spin Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.33277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive the dimensional reduction of 10D super Yang-Mills theory on a general closed 6D spin manifold using spectral decompositions for the higher-dimensional gauge field and gaugino, keeping the infinite towers of Kaluza-Klein (KK) modes in the lower-dimensional theory. We then calculate tree-level $2 \rightarrow 2$ scattering amplitudes with external massive spinors and vectors in this lower-dimensional theory. By studying the high-energy behavior of these amplitudes and imposing perturbative unitarity, we derive several sum rules that involve the eigenvalues of Laplace and Dirac operators on the internal 6-manifold, together with products of cubic coupling constants of the KK modes. These give concrete realizations of the known unitarity sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories. We illustrate explicitly how the simplest sum rule is satisfied for flat tori and round spheres.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Bertucci, James Bonifacio, Andrew Schrader

item.title: Machine Learning for Calabi--Yau Geometry and Heterotic Compactification
item.description: arXiv:2611.33311v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantitative predictions from string compactification depend on geometric data that are difficult to compute analytically. This review surveys machine learning approaches to predicting topological properties of Calabi-Yau manifolds, discusses the search for new Calabi-Yau fourfolds, as well as numerical methods for approximating Ricci-flat metrics. In the context of heterotic compactifications, we explain how bundle metrics and harmonic matter forms enter calculations of canonically normalized Yukawa couplings and axion-matter interactions. We also outline applications to flux compactifications, warped and corrected backgrounds, and geometric structures beyond the Calabi-Yau setting. Finally, we review available datasets and software, highlight connections with analytic methods, and discuss geometric constraints, numerical validation, and recent progress in rigorous error control.
item.dc:creator: Vishnu Jejjala, Damian Mayorga Pena

item.title: NuSrcAgent: An AI Agent for High-Energy Neutrino Source Searches
item.description: arXiv:2611.33324v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identifying the sources of high-energy cosmic neutrinos is crucial for understanding cosmic particle accelerators and probing new physics. IceCube provides public data that allow researchers to search independently for neutrino sources, but these analyses require substantial technical expertise and careful scientific choices. We present \system, the first publicly available AI agent for high-energy neutrino source searches. Compared to public likelihood codes, \system is easier to install and use, and supports more analysis types. To start an analysis, users need only specify a source or catalog. The agent takes natural-language requests, runs likelihood analyses on public IceCube event data, and saves the settings and calculation records so users can repeat the analyses. We demonstrate \system through single-source and catalog stacking analyses, obtaining results consistent with IceCube results. These examples also show its ability to search the literature, analyze non-power-law spectra using user-provided model code, and develop new analysis functions, such as signal-injection simulations. \system is also a powerful tool for improving and testing existing analysis code, as we demonstrate by using it to refine the background probability density functions and reduce residuals and spurious signal contributions in stacking analyses. \system makes high-energy neutrino data analysis more accessible to the broader research community. Code and usage instructions: \href{https://github.com/beizhouphys/NuSrcAgent}{\faGithub\ {\tt github.com/beizhouphys/NuSrcAgent}}.
item.dc:creator: Bei Zhou, Po-Wen Chang, Kohta Murase

item.title: Gradient-flow scale setting from octet baryon masses in N$^3$LO covariant chiral perturbation theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.33970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ by analyzing the lowest-lying octet-baryon masses on the Coordinated Lattice Simulations (CLS) $N_f=2+1$ ensembles in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory up to next-to-next-to-next-to leading order (N$^3$LO). By including the finite-volume corrections self-consistently and the discretization effects from Symanzik effective field theory, we obtain a good description of the RQCD data and determine the gradient-flow scale to be $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm with sub-percent precision. The predicted octet baryon masses agree well with the experimental values in the isospin limit. Using the Feynman-Hellmann theorem, we also estimate the nucleon sigma terms, which are consistent with direct determinations from three-point correlation functions on the same CLS ensembles.
item.dc:creator: Xiu-Lei Ren

item.title: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
item.description: arXiv:2611.34797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The origin of the Milky Way's high-energy neutrinos is debated. Their flavor composition reflects how they are made and could help settle it, but remains to be measured. We show that IceCube and KM3NeT, which see the inner Galaxy in complementary ways from opposite hemispheres, could start resolving its flavor composition in about a decade. With upcoming telescopes, they would infer the $\nu_e$ fraction at the sources to within 27%. A first comparison of Galactic and extragalactic flavor compositions could reveal strong magnetic fields in extragalactic sources or neutrino decay.
item.dc:creator: Mauricio Bustamante

item.title: Time-weighted energy correlators are infrared unsafe in gauge theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.34886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Energy correlators are infrared safe because each detector weights a parton by its energy, but a weight in the arrival time makes them infrared unsafe in gauge theories. For the state created by a scalar operator that makes two partons at lowest order in a weakly coupled conformal gauge theory, we show that the correlator of two time-weighted energy detectors (the light-ray operators $\int\!du\,u\,T_{uu}$) at separated directions diverges at two loops like the logarithm of the time window. The logarithm does not come from a single soft gluon, but from a soft parton pair with comparable energies, one parton in each detector; its coefficient is a closed-form function of the angle for any matter content. In $N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, we recover this coefficient from the two-gluon Regge term of the known four-point function and derive a simple relation to the logarithm in the charge correlator. In the planar theory the leading logarithms resum to a power of the window, set by the BFKL intercept.
item.dc:creator: Siqing Yu

item.title: Massive Triangle in Cosmological Correlator beyond Conformal Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.34892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A massive scalar coupled in pairs to the inflaton generates a one-loop primordial bispectrum whose mass corrections at generic momenta have lacked closed analytic expressions beyond conformal coupling. We obtain two leading mass corrections at arbitrary external momenta in terms of multiple polylogarithms of uniform weights three and four. Auxiliary-energy dressings preserve rational time integrals, revealing unexpected simplicity despite elliptic intermediate geometry. Independent full-loop evaluations, including blinded predictions, validate the closed forms. We also determine a subleading light-field singularity and recover the heavy-mass effective theory.
item.dc:creator: Taushif Ahmed, Syed Mehedi Hasan

item.title: Resonant top pair searches at the LHC: a window to electroweak phase transition
item.description: arXiv:2206.08381v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dynamics of electroweak phase transition could have profound consequences for particle physics and cosmology. We study the prospects for the HL-LHC to probe the strong first-order electroweak phase transition (SFOEWPT) regime in the type-I 2HDM. We focus on the Higgstrahlung channel $pp\to ZH/A$ with a resonant top-quark pair final state $H/A\to t\bar t$. We find that the top-quark pair final state renders the largest sensitivity to the SFOEWPT regime, in comparison to the other Higgstrahlung searches already performed by ATLAS and CMS, that focus on the $H/A\to bb$ and $H\to WW$ final states. We also derive the complementarity of the Higgstrahlung searches with other relevant classes of searches at the HL-LHC and compare them with the gravitational wave sensitivity at LISA.
item.dc:creator: Dorival Gon\c{c}alves, Ajay Kaladharan, Yongcheng Wu

item.title: Hadrons in group expansion
item.description: arXiv:2506.01272v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a general framework for describing symmetry-breaking responses in physical systems with approximate symmetries. Hadronic systems provide a particularly rich setting for investigating such symmetries. For example, the flavor $SU(4)$ symmetry involving the $u$, $d$, $s$, and $c$ quarks is severely broken, the flavor $SU(3)$ symmetry involving the $u$, $d$, and $s$ quarks is moderately broken, and the isospin $SU(2)$ symmetry involving the $u$ and $d$ quarks is only slightly broken. An important question is how a physical system responds to further symmetry breaking when its symmetry has already been partially broken. Motivated by the observed mass nonadditivity of vector mesons, we formulate this framework in terms of the group expansion, in which higher-order responses may modify the coefficients within the inherited response space or unlock additional independent response directions outside this space. We refer to these two effects as coefficient evolution and response unlocking, respectively, and develop a differential description connecting the interaction flow, mass flow, and state flow. We apply this framework to $J^P=1^-$ vector mesons and $J^P=3/2^+$ and $1/2^+$ baryons within flavor $SU(4)$ and $SU(5)$ reference spaces. These analyses illustrate how the internal structure and dynamics of a physical system, together with additional symmetries, can shape and constrain its symmetry-breaking responses. The group expansion thus provides a unified framework for organizing the evolution, correlations, and constraints of symmetry-breaking responses, with potential applications beyond hadronic systems.
item.dc:creator: Hua-Xing Chen

item.title: Study of anomalous charged triple gauge couplings with $W^-W^+$ process at $e^-e^+$ collider
item.description: arXiv:2512.06671v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study anomalous charged triple gauge couplings (aTGC) in $e^-e^+\to W^-W^+$ at $\sqrt{s}=250$~GeV with longitudinally polarized beams, parameterized by the five dimension-six operators $\mathcal{O}_{WWW}$, $\mathcal{O}_{W}$, $\mathcal{O}_{B}$, $\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{W}WW}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{W}}$ of the HISZ basis. All three decay channels, $\ell^\pm jj\slashed{E}$, $4j$ and $\ell^-\ell^+\slashed{E}$, are simulated explicitly at a leading-order including all diagrams that contribute to each final state and hence the interference of $W^-W^+$ with non-resonant amplitudes. The semi-leptonic signal is selected with cuts on $m_{j_1j_2}$ and $m_T^W$. The flavor identity of the two hardest light jets are classified as \emph{up}-type and \emph{down}-type jets with a dedicated boosted decision trees (BDT). In the $4j$ channel a multi-class BDT separates $W^-W^+$ from $ZZ$ and QCD production and the $W^\pm$ candidates are assigned using jet charge. In the dilepton channel $W^-W^+$ events are selected with cuts on $p_T^{\ell^-}$ and $m_{\ell^-\ell^+}$, and the two neutrino momenta are reconstructed analytically from the on-shell and beam-energy constraints. The cross section and 80 polarization and spin-correlation asymmetries in four disjoint bins of $\cos\theta_{W^-}$ are combined for both beam-polarization configurations through a covariance-based $\chi^2$. The two set of beam polarization offers an orthogonal cuts on parameter space leading to tighter bounds. The semi-leptonic and full-hadronic final states provides a competitive bounds on aTGCs, while full-leptonic offers the least sensitivity. Marginalized limits on aTGCs via. Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis for integrated luminosities for different values of integrated luminosities and systematic benchmarks are reported.
item.dc:creator: Amir Subba, Ritesh K. Singh

item.title: Lindblad-driven recombination of the X(3872) tetraquark
item.description: arXiv:2512.11539v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The internal structure of the exotic meson X(3872) remains an open question. We investigate its production in heavy-ion collisions under the hypothesis that it is a compact tetraquark. To this end, we derive a coalescence model from the Lindblad equation, assuming that unbound heavy quarks are thermalized within the quark-gluon plasma and that the adiabatic approximation holds. Using this model, we predict the nuclear modification factor of the X(3872) at LHC energies, with proton-proton baseline cross sections estimated from available experimental data. We also consider the effect of simplifying assumptions on the model, and a complementary approach based on chemical equilibration. Our results indicate that recombination is the dominant production mechanism for a tetraquark X(3872). It leads to a significant yield enhancement in heavy-ion collisions, suggesting that the nuclear modification factor is a powerful observable for probing the exotic nature of this state
item.dc:creator: N\'estor Armesto, Miguel \'Angel Escobedo, Elena G. Ferreiro, V\'ictor L\'opez-Pardo

item.title: Probing gluon saturation with forward di-hadron correlations in proton-nucleus collisions
item.description: arXiv:2512.21466v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a detailed numerical investigation of semi-inclusive forward di-hadron production in proton--nucleus collisions employing the Color Glass Condensate effective theory. We focus on the regime where di-hadrons are produced nearly back-to-back in the transverse plane, thereby justifying a transverse-momentum-dependent factorization approach in terms of small-$x$ gluon distributions. Our computation integrates several key elements: i) non-linear rapidity evolution via the Balitsky--Kovchegov equation with running coupling, ii) both perturbative and non-perturbative Sudakov resummation, and iii) a phenomenologically constrained model for the initial conditions for small-$x$ gluon distributions. We compare this phenomenological framework to experimental data from the STAR Collaboration on azimuthal correlations in forward di-pion production in both proton--proton and proton--gold collisions. We analyze the systematic theoretical uncertainties associated with the saturation scales of nuclei at the initial scale for rapidity evolution and with those associated with the hadronization process. Finally, we make predictions for the kinematics anticipated to be covered by the ALICE Forward Calorimeter (FoCal) upgrade at the Large Hadron Collider.
item.dc:creator: Paul Caucal, Zhong-Bo Kang, Piotr Korcyl, Farid Salazar, Bj\"orn Schenke, Tomasz Stebel, Raju Venugopalan, Wenbin Zhao

item.title: Critical fluctuation patterns and anisotropic correlations driven by temperature gradients
item.description: arXiv:2603.04923v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Studies of QCD phase transition signals are often conducted under spatially uniform temperature conditions. However, the influence of spatial temperature gradients on the signals emerging at the phase interface in the fireball generated by heavy-ion collisions has not yet been fully explored. Based on an Ising-like effective potential, we study the locally equilibrated systems with temperature gradients. In a 2D disk geometry, the low-energy fluctuation spectrum is explicitly resolved into radial and angular momentum modes. The nonlocal correaltions of singular eigen-mode exhibits strong anisotropy, which are long-ranged along isotherms but suppressed radially due to the thermal geometry of the system. Unlike homogeneous systems where the zero-momentum mode dominates, correlations in such inhomogeneous system result from the superposition of a series of zero and non-zero angular momentum modes with comparable contributions. We extract the singular angular momentum modes and establish their connection to experimentally observable anisotropic flow. We find azimuthally sensitive observables may offer a previously unexplored avenue for detecting the QCD phase transition.
item.dc:creator: Lijia Jiang, Tao Yang, Jun-Hui Zheng

item.title: Dark matter in classically conformal theories: WIMP and supercooling
item.description: arXiv:2603.09126v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Beyond solving the hierarchy problem, classically conformal (CC) theories naturally accommodate dark matter (DM). In this work, we explore the CC $SU(2)_X$ gauge theory with a triplet dark scalar, uncovering two distinct DM scenarios: weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) and supercooled DM. The production mechanisms are strongly influenced by the CC model's unique first-order phase transition evolution history, which differs significantly from those in non-conformal models. We obtain the viable parameter space for each scenario and investigate the current constraints and future sensitivities at experiments, demonstrating that gravitational wave signals from the phase transition provide a common detection channel for both the WIMP and supercooled DM regimes.
item.dc:creator: Ke-Pan Xie, Cheng-Hao Zhan

item.title: Light-by-light scattering: asymptotic expansions, Coulomb resummation and NLO corrections
item.description: arXiv:2604.00099v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Light-by-light (LbL) scattering is one of the earliest predictions of quantum electrodynamics (QED). Interest in this process has been renewed following its experimental observation at the LHC and the prospects of future measurements at free-electron laser facilities. In this paper, we refine theoretical predictions for LbL scattering by improving the full fermion-mass-dependent two-loop QCD and QED helicity amplitudes using high- and low-energy asymptotic expansions, and by performing Coulomb resummation in the threshold region. The $W$-boson contribution, relevant when the di-photon invariant mass exceeds twice the $W$-boson mass, is included at one-loop accuracy. We present state-of-the-art predictions for LbL cross sections in the Standard Model and provide a new event generator, LbLatNLO, for Monte Carlo simulations of LbL scattering.
item.dc:creator: Ajjath A H, Ekta Chaubey, Hua-Sheng Shao
